subjects.label: Ubisoft Connect launcher and account
subjects.description: The publisher's own launcher sitting between Steam and the game: being forced to install Ubisoft Connect, it surviving an uninstall, losing access to an account, key activation and login failures, and cloud-save syncing that stalls; general grumbling about DRM elsewhere does not belong.

subjects.label: Season passes and editions
subjects.description: The stack of year passes, season passes and gold or complete editions this game sells, how much they add, which expansions are worth it, and regretting the base game alone; plain remarks about the sticker price without reference to passes or editions do not belong.

subjects.label: Lost nights and addiction
subjects.description: Hours vanishing, playing through the night, skipping sleep or school, twelve-hour sittings and ignoring the game's own reminder to take a break; a plain statement that the game is fun does not belong.

subjects.label: Production chains across islands and regions
subjects.description: Building and rebalancing goods chains, shipping between islands, juggling several regions and continents at once and the spreadsheet-like mental load of keeping every need met; talk of what a city looks like or of fighting rivals does not belong.

subjects.label: Navy, AI rivals and diplomacy
subjects.description: The military and diplomatic layer on top of the city builder: warships and fleets, AI competitors, being unable to leave a war, having ships sunk, and whether beating opponents is the point at all; the economic competition of trade routes does not belong.

subjects.label: Exploiting and oppressing your citizens
subjects.description: Relishing the game as an industrial-era tyrant: starving citizens and policing their protests, poisoning richer residents with smelter smoke and railways, and colonial exploitation played for laughs; earnest remarks about balancing citizen needs do not belong.

subjects.label: Place in the Anno series
subjects.description: Comparing this entry to earlier games in the same series, calling it the best of the franchise or a return to how the old ones felt, and the series' standing as a landmark of the genre; comparisons to games outside the series belong to genre.

subjects.label: The city up close
subjects.description: Walking through the finished city at ground level, how the detail holds up once you zoom in rather than from above, and the lines citizens say as you pass; general praise for the visuals from the usual view does not belong.
